a: Amortized analysis averages costly operations over a sequence (e.g. dynamic array resize).
Master theorem solves many divide-and-conquer recurrences of form T(n)=aT(n/b)+f(n).
NP-complete problems are hard; no known polynomial algorithm for all, but verifiable quickly.
Approximation algorithms find near-optimal answers for hard optimization problems.
Greedy works when local optimal choices lead to a global optimum.
A problem has optimal substructure if optimal solutions contain optimal subsolutions.
Memoization is top-down caching; tabulation is bottom-up DP tables.
Using more memory can reduce time (and vice versa).
Comparison sorting requires Ω(n log n) comparisons in the worst case.
Good hash tables give expected O(1) average operations.
